run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request ID the customer quoted is fully resolvable in the log store: REQ-EU-8K4M2 appears in exactly one document, an ERROR log from the 'auth' service in region eu-west at 2026-11-18T14:52:47Z on endpoint /api/v2/auth/validate, stating the request took 15847ms and that the LDAP backend connection pool was exhausted, so the customer's authentication failed after retries. That is the only ERROR document in the whole app-185-geo-* log set in the authorized window, and eu-west auth is the only region/service combination in the logs with latency above the 150ms baseline (max 15847ms vs 150ms everywhere else in Europe and the other four regions). So the failing component evidenced here is the auth service in eu-west, not a region-wide slowdown and not the Kubernetes otel-demo workloads (no workload named auth exists there, all 32 pods Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no events, and every flagd fault-injection flag is off). Conclusion is partial because the deeper dependency named by the error (the LDAP backend) is not instrumented anywhere I could query, and Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) so latency/error-rate corroboration was not possible; the log set itself is daily-sampled, so whether the auth slowdown was a single request or sustained cannot be established.

claims.text: Request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 appears in exactly one document in app-185-geo-* within 2026-10-24T17:31:16Z–2026-11-23T17:31:16Z: @timestamp 2026-11-18T14:52:47Z, index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, level ERROR, service=auth, region=eu-west, endpoint=/api/v2/auth/validate, response_time_ms=15847, user_id=customer-39284, message 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.'

That document is the only ERROR-level log in the app-185-geo-* set in the authorized window: a terms aggregation over level.keyword returned INFO 1620 and ERROR 1, and the single ERROR message bucket is the auth timeout above, with the only region bucket eu-west and only service bucket auth.

For service=auth, eu-west has 11 documents with min response_time_ms 150, avg 1577 and max 15847 plus 1 ERROR document, while the other five regions (ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east, us-west) each have 10 documents with max response_time_ms 150 and 0 ERROR documents.

The eu-west auth baseline in the same data is 150ms: ten daily INFO 'Request completed successfully' documents with response_time_ms 150 span 2026-11-14T17:29:00Z to 2026-11-23T17:29:00Z, and the 15847ms request at 2026-11-18T14:52:47Z is roughly 105x that baseline.

No other service in Europe is elevated in these logs: in eu-west all 26 other services (analytics, api, billing, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist, worker) have max response_time_ms 150, and in eu-central all 27 services including auth have max response_time_ms 150.

The Kubernetes cluster contains no workload named auth: the 24 deployments across all namespaces are kube-system (coredns, metrics-server), local-path-storage (local-path-provisioner) and otel-demo (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart), and all 32 observed pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination reason.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in namespace otel-demo (key demo.flagd.json) defines fault/latency flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off' (0 or false in effect); no flag refers to auth.

No ldap/directory/idp/sso index exists in the log store (a filtered index listing returned an empty list), and no service named auth or ldap is in the trace service inventory supplied for this run, so the auth service and its LDAP backend are not visible as Kubernetes objects or trace services in the explored systems.

The slow, failed request REQ-EU-8K4M2 is attributable to the auth service's LDAP backend connection pool being exhausted at 2026-11-18T14:52:47Z, as the error text states; this is a hypothesis at dependency depth because no LDAP pool metric, trace or log is available to confirm the pool's state or what exhausted it.

The auth latency event may be a single isolated request rather than a sustained degradation: the only samples available are one log document per service per day at a flat 150ms, including auth in eu-west at 2026-11-18T17:29:00Z (about 2.5 hours after the error) and at 2026-11-19T17:29:00Z, so duration and breadth of the slowdown are unresolved.

Feature-flag fault injection in the otel-demo cluster is rejected as the cause of this request: every flag in flagd-config is at defaultVariant 'off', no flag targets an auth service, and no workload named auth exists in the cluster.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, verify auth /api/v2/auth/validate latency and error rate around 2026-11-18T14:52Z, and pull the auth service's LDAP connection-pool metrics (exhaustion/wait timeouts) and the LDAP directory server's health for that window to confirm or refute the pool-exhaustion explanation.

Request a higher-resolution auth access log (current log set carries only one document per service per day) to count how many eu-west requests exceeded the 150ms baseline at 2026-11-18T14:52Z and whether the pool exhaustion recurred.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every query attempted (get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no latency, error-rate or pool metric could corroborate the log evidence for 2026-11-18T14:52:47Z.

Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace of REQ-EU-8K4M2 or of the auth call chain was obtained; the service list supplied for this run does not contain auth at all, so the log-derived auth service cannot be mapped to a traced service.

The auth service is not a Kubernetes object in this cluster (no deployment, pod or service named auth), so its pod status, restarts, container configuration and events could not be checked; the app-185-geo-* log indices and the otel-demo cluster appear to be different systems.

The LDAP backend named in the error is not observable: no index name matches ldap/directory/idp/sso, and no LDAP pool metric, trace or log was found, so the deeper cause (pool size/limit, capacity, upstream LDAP slowness) is unverified and its owning object cannot be named.

Log coverage is sparse and bounded: all 1620 INFO documents cover only 2026-11-14T17:29:00Z to 2026-11-23T17:29:00Z at one document per service per day, so whether the auth slowdown was a single request or sustained, and how many other requests were affected, is unknown.
Kubernetes events over the authorized window returned no_data (zero events), so there is no cluster-side event evidence for the incident period.
Change history for the auth service or its LDAP dependency is not available in this run (change_history is not integrated), so no change/rollout can be linked to the event.
next_steps: Retrieve auth service and LDAP pool telemetry (latency percentile, timeout/error counters, pool wait and exhaustion gauges) for 2026-11-18T14:00–16:00Z from the auth platform's own monitoring once Prometheus/Jaeger access is restored.
Review the auth service's LDAP connection-pool configuration (max pool size, acquire timeout, retry policy) and the LDAP directory server's health at 2026-11-18T14:52Z.
Obtain the full eu-west auth access log from 2026-11-18 rather than the daily samples, to size how many customers beyond user customer-39284 were affected.
Consider alerting on auth response_time_ms > 1s per region using the app-185-geo-* logs or equivalent, since the current dataset records only one document per service per day.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
